title: Verifier Feedback and Model Collaboration Under Matched Call Budgets
content: Exact verifiers reject invalid outputs, but detailed feedback and model collaboration require strong revision controls. We study directed-path construction and Boolean-program synthesis with complete executable checks. An original frozen protocol uses 48 development tasks and 256 deduplicated test tasks to select configurations for independent sampling, validity-only refinement, and exact-feedback refinement. Each matched strategy receives three calls with the same completion-token cap. Exact feedback solves 117/256 tasks, compared with 115 for validity feedback, 78 for independent sampling, and 106 for mixed-model refinement. Neither conservative primary interval establishes the prespecified five-point advantage, and a serving abort independently activates the exclusion rule. A separately declared full-panel follow-up replaces Llama with Mistral and collects fresh responses from all configurations on the same tasks. All 4,848 requests complete without serving errors. Gemma exact feedback solves 115 tasks versus 88 for development-selected Mistral validity, but the matched Gemma validity control solves 111. Mixed refinement also solves 111. The larger cross-configuration contrast therefore cannot establish the value of detailed feedback alone. Exact classical algorithms solve all tasks, while repeated identical requests to retained configurations do not always yield identical served text. The original comparison remains ineligible, and the reused-panel follow-up is descriptive. Together, the studies separate revision, feedback detail, model selection, operational behavior, and resource accounting without establishing a general collaboration advantage.
